title: Activation grease & fail-open procedures (canary + A/B) - working notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for the activation "grease" steps and explicit fail-open procedures used during canaries and A/B runs for latency-sensitive LLM features. The focus is operational choreography: what humans do before, during, and after a canary slice when traffic needs to be eased or fully opened.

Scope:
- Applies to staged rollouts that route user traffic to new model variants, rerankers, or orchestration changes (routing policies).
- Covers small-batch canaries (0.1%–5%), medium (5%–25%), and broad A/B experiments.
- Coexists with automated circuit-breakers; this doc defines human playbook + safe fail-open semantics.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) Pre-flight: smoke + synthetic probe suite, capacity check, oncall alignment, comms slots.
2) Activation grease: warm caches, parallel dry-run logging, metric shadowing for 30m.
3) Stepwise exposure: spine slices (0.1 -> 1 -> 5 -> 20) with 15–60m observation windows.
4) Fail-open ladder: soft-fallback -> full-fallback -> traffic cutover to baseline. Each step has scripted notifications and rollback commands.

Checklist: pre-flight items (notes to self):
- [ ] Synthetic probes green for 3 consecutive runs (latency P95 within target).
- [ ] Cost impact estimate for 1-hour at each slice (console estimate runbook).
- [ ] Canaries queued in release calendar + calendar invite for stakeholders (ops, product, SRE).
- [ ] Slack channel #rollout-ops-<feature> created and pinned runbook snippet.
- [ ] Oncall assigned to watch telemetry for the window; escalation owner named.

Activation grease steps (detailed):
- 00:00 — Warmup: send 10k synthetic prefix requests to populate KV cache and embeddings cache. Tag requests with test_id.
- 00:10 — Shadow logging mode: route 0% traffic but mirror real requests to variant for logging only (no responses). Compare token-level latencies and token counts.
- 00:30 — Dry-run scoring: run offline reranker on last 1k actual requests and compare outputs to baseline. Capture distributional diffs.
- 00:45 — Quick manual review: product + applied ml on anomalies found in offline run. Decide proceed/hold.

Stepwise exposure template (example):
- Step A: 0.1% (duration 30m) -> check: p50/p95 latency, error rate, user-visible errors, cost-per-request delta, quality regressions from evalset.
- Step B: 1% (duration 45m) -> add: conversion metric sanity check, sampling for human review on 1/100 requests.
- Step C: 5% (duration 60m) -> monitor upstream services (DB, cache), increase sampling to 1/20 for human-in-loop.
- Step D: 20% (duration 120m) -> verify stability at scale, review longer-tail metrics, confirm no oscillation.

Human-in-loop sampling play:
- Sampling rate and workflow: for small slices sample 1/200 requests; for medium 1/50; for large 1/20. Samples go to a shared Loom + issue template with: input, baseline response, variant response, token-level cost, and quick tag (acceptable / needs-fix / safety).
- Reviewer rotation: 2-hour shifts, minimum one ML reviewer and one product reviewer on rotation.

Fail-open ladder (explicit commands and intent):
1) Soft-fallback (route failing route for specific slice): reduces variant weight to baseline baseline-preserving % while keeping variant live for logging. Command: console set-weight --route <route> --variant <variant> --pct <new_pct>. Notify channel with reason.
2) Partial cut (close variant for new requests, allow in-flight completions): console pause-variant --route <route> --variant <variant> --drain=true.
3) Full fail-open (switch entire route to baseline model): console redirect-route --route <route> --to <baseline-model-version> --force. This must be accompanied by incident page and stakeholder ping.
4) Re-open sequence: incrementally re-run activation grease with new constraints once root cause fixed and postmortem agreed.

Observation signals and SLO thresholds to watch (operational):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 token and request latencies (alert if p95 increases by >30% vs baseline).
- Errors: 5xx, model timeouts, token truncation errors (alert if error-rate > 0.5%).
- Quality: top-line metric (CTR, conversion, or task-specific success). Alert if quality delta > 3% negative.
- Cost: token-cost-per-request delta > 25% -> meet with product to confirm runway.
- Drift: prompt-level hallucination score (from eval runner). Manual review trigger if hallucination score increases 0.5pt on 5k-sample.

Suggested console queries (pseudocode snippets for SRE / observability):
- Latency slices: SELECT percentile(lat_ms, 50), percentile(lat_ms,95) FROM requests WHERE route='X' AND variant='canary' AND ts > now()-30m GROUP BY 1m
- Error spike: count(errors) BY minute WHERE variant='canary' AND ts > now()-15m
- Cost delta: sum(tokens*unit_cost) GROUP BY variant for window 1h
(Replace with actual query language in the observability playbook.)

Communication scripts (short templates):
- When stepping up: "Stepping canary up: route=<route> variant=<variant> -> pct=<new_pct>. Observing 30m windows. Watch #rollout-ops-<feature>. Contact oncall @<name> for immediate hold."
- When triggering soft-fallback: "Soft-fallback initiated at <time>. Reason: <metric>. Command: <cmd>. Expected impact: reduces variant exposure to <pct>. Will monitor 15m then decide next step."
- When full fail-open: "Fail-open executed. Route switched to <baseline-model>. Incident created: <incident-url>. Postmortem owner: <name>. Do not re-open without org signoff."

Simulation scenarios to rehearse (for tabletop runs):
- Scenario 1 (latency surge): synthetic workload increases queueing; p95 doubles. Walk through soft-fallback -> pause -> fail-open. Time budget: 30 min.
- Scenario 2 (quality regression): human reviewers flag 5% of samples with safety tags. Immediate hold -> batch rollback -> incident trigger. Time budget: 45 min.
- Scenario 3 (partial regional outage): traffic routing fails to fallback regionally; test cross-region routing policy and degraded mode.

Decision record (scratchpad):
- 2025-01-20: agreed sampling rates and human rota (Maya + Daniel).
- 2025-01-29: increase activation shadow window to 30m after observing cold-cache flakiness.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to automate initial 'grease' warmup without incurring large costs? (action: infra to prototype low-cost synthetic runner).
- Should we standardize a single CLI for all rollout operations (console already has partial commands; need to finalize args)? (action: engineering - PR #872).
- Define exact tagging schema for sampled requests so analytics can filter reliably.

Notes to self / rough heuristics (informal):
- Keep first slice small when exposing model architecture changes (0.05% if possible).
- Prefer soft-fallback over immediate full cut when possible — keeps variant available for debugging traces.
- Time windows scale with traffic volume; lower-volume services require longer windows.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Incident template: link above (Confluence).
- Human review issue template: copy to channel and paste the header: "INPUT / BASELINE / VARIANT / COST / SAFETY TAG / OP NOTES".

End notes: this is intentionally a messy, operational notebook. Use it as a starting script for the rollout rehearsal. We will extract a cleaner runbook after 3 successful rehearsals and one real canary.

-- Maya
